claims.claim: Germany's mandatory deposit on one-way cans and bottles for beer, mineral water and carbonated drinks began on 1 January 2003 under Environment Minister Jürgen Trittin.
claims.episode_span: On 1 January 2003, Environment Minister Jürgen Trittin’s new deposit rule took effect on single-use cans and bottles for beer, mineral water and carbonated soft drinks.
claims.supporting_quote: Damit wird die Pfandpflicht für Dosen und Einwegflaschen zum 1. Januar 2003 ausgelöst.

claims.claim: At the C1000 supermarket in Vaals, sales of Cola cans rose from 24,500 to 46,800 pallets year-over-year after the German deposit began.
claims.episode_span: In Vaals on the Dutch border, the C1000 supermarket recorded cola-can volume jumping from 24,500 to 46,800 pallets in a single year.
claims.source_title: „Die kommen in Scharen und holen die Dosen”
claims.supporting_quote: one store reporting sales of Cola cans rising from 24,500 to 46,800 pallets year-over-year

claims.claim: Stores in Słubice reported up to 70 percent sales increases in deposit-free single-use drinks after 1 January 2003, with customers traveling from Berlin.
claims.episode_span: One small Polish store reported that German customers routinely bought ten bottles each, and larger supermarkets saw overall sales of deposit-free drinks rise by as much as 70 percent.
claims.source_title: Nach der Einfuhr des Dosenpfandes: Deutsche kaufen ihre Getränke in Polen
claims.supporting_quote: Die Läden melden bis 70 Prozent Plus.
